issues.legal_issue: A civil court retains jurisdiction over a validly instituted eviction suit when rent-control protection is extended to the premises during the suit, unless the legislation specifically protects terminated tenancies or pending proceedings.
material_facts: The premises were outside the rent legislation when the landlord instituted the eviction suit after terminating the tenancy.
During the suit, a notification brought the area containing the premises within the rent legislation.
The trial court decreed eviction, and the tenant challenged the decree on the ground that the civil court lost jurisdiction when the notification took effect.
The applicable legislation contained no provision protecting ex-tenants in these circumstances or excluding civil-court jurisdiction over pending suits.
issues.conclusion: The civil court retained jurisdiction to decide the suit. The appeal was allowed, the judgments of the appellate court and High Court were set aside, and the trial court’s decree was restored.
issues.legal_principle: The parties’ rights ordinarily crystallise when a valid suit is instituted, and later application of rent-control legislation does not oust the civil court’s jurisdiction over that suit absent a specific statutory provision extending protection to terminated tenancies or pending proceedings. This follows the reasoning in Atma Ram Mittal v. Ishwar Singh Punia, Vineet Kumar v. Mangal Sain Wadhera, Ram Saroop Rai v. Lilawati, Shri Kishan alias Krishna Kumar v. Manoj Kumar, and Mansoor Khan v. Moti Ram. The Court distinguished Mani Subrat Jain v. Raja Ram Vohra and Lakshmi Narayan Guin v. Niranjan Modak because the relevant legislation there defined tenants to include ex-tenants and expressly protected against eviction under earlier decrees. The Court considered Sections 1(3) and 13(1) of the Haryana Rent Urban (Control of Rent and Eviction) Act, 1973, and the absence of a provision ousting civil-court jurisdiction over validly instituted suits.

rule.if: eviction_suit_in_civil_court and suit_filed_before_rent_protection and premises_later_brought_under_rent_protection and not statute_protects_terminated_tenancies_in_pending_suits

predicates.eviction_suit_in_civil_court: A landlord instituted a suit in a civil court seeking eviction of a tenant.
predicates.suit_filed_before_rent_protection: The premises were not covered by rent-control protection when the eviction suit was instituted.
predicates.premises_later_brought_under_rent_protec: During the pending suit, a legal change brought the premises within rent-control protection.
predicates.statute_protects_terminated_tenancies_in: The applicable legislation specifically protects terminated tenancies or pending proceedings from civil-court eviction jurisdiction.

issues.definition: When a civil eviction suit is filed before the premises receive rent-control protection and that protection is extended during the suit, the civil court retains jurisdiction unless the legislation specifically protects terminated tenancies in pending suits.
